final.title: Late payment terms are a workflow problem, not just finance
final.body:
Late payment terms usually show up as a workflow problem before they show up as a finance problem. For an owner-operator, the useful question is not “are the terms bad?” but “which recurring task is creating the drag: invoice tracking, payment-chasing emails, or an aging report in a spreadsheet?” That is the bounded decision worth making first.

The representative persona decision here is simple: compare the cost of keeping it manual, hiring help, or automating one repeatable step. If the task changes too much from case to case, or if the step touches money movement, keep human approval in place and leave it manual. That is policy, not a failure.

If the workflow is repeatable, measurable, and mostly the same each time, it may be a candidate for AI or workflow automation. Bareni’s normal sequence is a free diagnostic, then a one-page pilot proposal, then a working MVP; those timings are intended scopes, not guarantees, and the diagnostic can also say plainly that AI is not the right fit.

A practical next step: write down the last five overdue-payment cases and ask one question about each one — was the follow-up the same every time? Dry, but useful.
